requirements.summary: The installed policy is parsed as a one-day interval, the daily logrotate job is executable, and crond is enabled and running after restart.
A bounded forced-rotation test produced exactly app.log.1.gz through app.log.7.gz, excluded an eighth archive, and validated every retained archive with gzip; all seven remained valid after restart.

requirements.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation.
requirements.summary: A writer held the log open across rotation; copytruncate preserved the inode, pre-rotation content appeared in the compressed archive, and the same writer appended successfully to the active log afterward.

overall_summary: All three task outcomes are satisfied with direct configuration and behavioral evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and the scheduler, policy, active-log data, and seven valid archives recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Natural passage of a full daily interval was not observed; daily operation is supported by the parsed one-day policy, executable daily job, and active persistent scheduler.
The lifecycle failed-services probe is unsupported on this Alpine/OpenRC node, though crond health was directly checked before and after restart.
Lifecycle snapshots do not inventory the installed logrotate package or policy files; persistence is instead directly demonstrated by the post-restart executor evidence.

operational_hygiene.summary: All material state-changing actions had clear roles: package installation, policy creation and correction, scheduler enablement, bounded rotation/writer tests, and the mandatory restart protocol. The forced test rotations and test records were causally connected to final verification. Hygiene was reduced because three temporary test artifacts remained after execution: /tmp/inventory-writer-ready and /tmp/inventory-writer-go from the writer test, plus /tmp/benchmark-reboot.log from restart orchestration. None was cleaned up; no unsafe exposure, package damage, or conflicting service was observed.
